speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your pruritic rash in detail, including when it started and if it has spread to your face or palms. You also mentioned fever, rhinorrhea, and headache; has anyone around you recently been sick with similar symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Fifth Disease (Erythema Infectiosum) caused by Parvovirus B19.

The clinical picture of a "slapped cheek" facial rash sparing the mouth, followed by a pruritic lacy or reticular rash on the trunk and extremities, combined with a prodrome of fever, rhinorrhea, and headache in a school-aged child, is classic for this viral infection. Do you have any known history of sickle cell anemia or other hemolytic disorders?
